RQ1.title: DETERMINISM
RQ1.question: Does the OSM→OpenDRIVE pipeline preserve stable structural and topological signatures under fixed inputs, and where does byte-level nondeterminism arise?
required_inputs: frozen osm2odr + pipeline code state at production SHA
RQ1.required_experiment: Three repeated Osm2Odr runs under fixed inputs; raw hash + normalized hash + structural signature comparison
RQ1.required_falsification: Any single run producing a different structural signature (road/junction/length topology) under identical pinned inputs
RQ1.current_state: AUTHORITATIVE for structural repeatability and raw byte non-repeatability; BOUNDED for timestamp-normalized byte equality. Three runs confirm structural stability; timestamp metadata identified as byte-level source. Large-artifact re-gen pending clean clone.

RQ2.title: STRUCTURAL DOMAIN GAP
RQ2.question: How do automatically generated OSM-based CARLA maps differ structurally from a manually modeled CARLA map of the same region?
RQ2.required_code_state: ultimate_pipeline at integration/production-large-map-20260918 (SHA 65eb0f14); local_registration.py and frechet_gap.py pinned to registry-resolved auto map
RQ2.required_experiment: Local hull-footprint structural comparison (road length, junction, road count ratios, curvature, lane width, building density, Fréchet distance) auto vs manual within manual map footprint
RQ2.required_falsification: Local hull-footprint road-length ratio reverting to uncropped whole-map scale (>10x) or Fréchet distance exceeding prior recomputed bounds under same pinned maps
RQ2.current_state: BOUNDED with corrected local (manual-map-footprint) comparison as primary result. Hull footprint ratios: road-length 2.683x, junction 3.782x, road-count 3.561x. Fréchet: mean 58.18m, median 36.13m, p90 140.48m (894 pairs). Re-verified 2026-09-17 against current map-of-record pin.

RQ4.title: STRUCTURAL VARIABILITY AND LATENT REPRESENTATION
RQ4.question: Does repeated automatic generation from the same pinned inputs introduce measurable structural variability, and can a latent representation of that variability support robustness analysis?
required_inputs: 5-seed GNN ensemble (seeds 42-46, 562 union tiles, 50 epochs, batch 16, lr 1e-4, CPU)
RQ4.required_code_state: ultimate_pipeline at integration/production-large-map-20260918 (SHA 65eb0f14); run_gnn_pipeline.py with leak exclusion active
RQ4.required_experiment: 5-seed GNN retrain with leak-exclusion; cosine distance + bootstrap CI; pre-training and post-hoc leakage audits; k-sweep; explicit DR wiring verification
RQ4.required_falsification: Leakage audit FAIL on any seed checkpoint, or cosine_distance CI including zero
RQ4.current_state: AUTHORITATIVE (leak-free, 2026-09-24). 5-seed ensemble: cosine_distance mean 0.9207 (95% CI [0.845, 0.976]), CI excludes zero across all 5 seeds. Pre-training and post-hoc leakage audits PASS (eval_pair_hash_overlap=[] for all seeds). Explicit DR wiring confirmed.

critical_rule: A newly found issue becomes thesis-blocking ONLY if at least one is true: (1) it can materially change an RQ result; (2) it can cause the wrong artifact/map/dataset/model to be evaluated; (3) it can make an experiment non-reproducible; (4) it prevents required execution; (5) it invalidates provenance or train/test separation. Everything else becomes POST_THESIS_TECH_DEBT.
